uncertain_decisions.component: Co-locating Visit and VisitController in owner-service instead of creating an independent visit service, chosen because Visit is packaged under org.springframework.samples.petclinic.owner and lacks its own repository in the component catalog.
uncertain_decisions.reason: Co-locating Visit and VisitController in owner-service instead of creating an independent visit service, chosen because Visit is packaged under org.springframework.samples.petclinic.owner and lacks its own repository in the component catalog.

unsupported_assumptions: Assumed Visit persistence lifecycle is managed through OwnerRepository or cascade operations, as no VisitRepository is present in the evidence catalog.
Assumed no direct static calls or foreign keys between Vet and Visit/Owner, as relational and call data are omitted under condition E0_MINIMAL.
architectural_risks: Potential high coupling inside owner-service if visits scale at a significantly higher write rate than owner profiles.
Data model entanglement if Visit records require veterinarian references that cannot be enforced via monolithic foreign keys post-migration.
critique: A two-service decomposition aligns cleanly with existing Java package structure (vet vs. owner). However, grouping visits with owners and pets may limit independent scalability of visit scheduling; extraction of a dedicated visit service should be evaluated when call graph and persistence evidence become available.

migration_priority.reason: Clear module boundary (org.springframework.samples.petclinic.vet), self-contained persistence and presentation, with no dependencies on client or visit tracking.
Core business domain containing multiple related entities (Owner, Pet, PetType, Visit); higher internal complexity and transaction scope.

notes: Parsed from LLM JSON. Gold labels were not in the prompt.
